title: 知能情報プログラミングⅠ
subtitle: Intelligent Information Programming I
keywords: expressions and operations 2.variables and data types 3.conditional statements 4.loops 5.functions
educationalGoal: The goal of this course is to be able to write and execute basic computer programs in Python which is often used in data science and AI. By completing this course, students are expected to obtain skills to setup an appropriate development environment on their PC, to write basic Python programs, and to execute them.
advice: In Intelligent Information Programming I (this course) and the subsequent course, Intelligent Information Programming II, students will learn how to write programs in Python to accomplish certain tasks. This introductory course covers the following topics. (1) How to install software necessary for developing programs in Python and running them. (2) How to edit and save programs written in Python and execute them. (3) How to combine basic building blocks of Python to accomplish certain tasks. For (3), students will have a lot of opportunities to engage in hands-on exercises where they can acquire working knowledge of computer programming.
requiredKnowledge: There is no prerequisite course for Intelligent Information Programming I. Students have to bring a PC, an AC adapter, and a network cable to the class due to exercises where students are asked to write programs and upload them during class hours for later grading. It is required to be able to turn on PC, to shutdown PC, and to type on the keyboard. The network connection permmission is also required until the 3rd week.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain what operations it takes to run a program.
Be able to assign various values to variables, and to use the print function to display their contents.
Be able to write expressions combining properly named variables and operators, and to evaluate them.
Be able to define lists and tuples, and to write programs that use them.
Be able to use control flow structures such as conditional statements and loops in writing programs.
Be able to define functions for relatively simple tasks.

achievementLevels.ideal: In addition to the standard achievement levels on the right: (7) Be able to write clean and readable programs. (8) Be able to write more complex programs, for instance, with nested control flows.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Be able to setup development environment on their PC and execute programs using it. (2) Be able to use variables: assign values to them and then evaluate them. (3) Be able to write appropriate expressions using variables and operators. (4) Be able to write programs using lists and tuples. (5) Be able to use if, for and while statements. (6) Be able to write simple functions.
